text:
In 2025, Vietnamese consumers spent $2.1 billion ordering food online, marking a 19% year-on-year increase driven by rapid urbanization and a cultural shift toward convenience. Despite having the smallest overall market size among tracked Southeast Asian countries, Vietnam is currently the fastest-growing food delivery market in the region.

📊 Market Breakdown

Metric
2025 Status & Performance
Market Size
$2.1 Billion gross merchandise value (GMV).
Growth Rate
19% YoY growth (up from $1.8 billion in 2024).
Regional Dominance
Ho Chi Minh City
Future Forecast
Projected to expand at a 13.58% CAGR, reaching $3.22 billion by 2033.

🔎 Competitive Landscape: The Duopoly

The market has completely consolidated into a strict duopoly. Following a brutal price war, major competitors like South Korea's Baemin (exited Dec 2023), Indonesia's GoFood (exited Sept 2024), and local startup Loship (exited late 2024) collapsed or withdrew from the country.

ShopeeFood & GrabFood: Jointly command a massive 96% of the total market share.
ShopeeFood: Holds the slight edge with roughly 49% to 56% share of orders, leveraging its integrated e-commerce ecosystem and ShopeePay mobile wallet.
GrabFood: Follows closely at 36% to 42% market share, utilizing its robust ride-hailing network and multi-service ecosystem.
BeFood: Stands as the small remaining alternative with roughly 9% market share.

💡 Evolving Consumer Dynamics

Group Ordering Over Solo Dining: Food delivery has shifted from solo meals to a social experience. 84% of urban users order for groups of 2 to 3 people, often sharing meals at work or at home.
Zero Brand Loyalty: On average, urban consumers actively use 1.7 delivery apps to cross-shop for the steepest discounts and fastest shipping times.
Comfort and Coffee Culture: The highest volume of cart items consists of bubble tea (31%), fast food (28%), and traditional rice dishes (21%).
Infrastructure Shift: The rapid adoption of mobile wallets, government-backed digital payment initiatives, and the optimization of motorcycle courier networks are keeping transaction friction exceptionally low.
